sonnet.problem: The right answer is the only negative one, and its form differs from the two wrong answers, which are matching positive 'A nation ... by all' lines. Wrong answers like 'honored by all' are not believable for people provoking God, so the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

sonnet.problem: The right answer is the only positive description of life. The two wrong answers are both hardship, so the tone differs and the right answer stands out.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

sonnet.problem: 'Did the LORD not overlook all that incense' can be read as meaning the same as 'did the LORD not remember', since both ask whether He took notice. A baker could argue it is right.
sonnet.rule: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

sonnet.problem: The card says the sign is about Pharaoh Hophra. Verse 29 says the sign is that the LORD will punish them 'in this place', and the text does not say the Pharaoh line in verse 30 is the sign. The card fixes a connection the text leaves open.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The statement repeats the fact card 17 just asked, that Hophra will be handed over to his enemies. It adds only the Zedekiah comparison, so it is a second question on the same point.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question. ... A True statement never just repeats the card before it.
